newsitem.title: JAPAN: TENNIS-WIND FAILS TO DETER KRAJICEK.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WIND FAILS TO DETER KRAJICEK.

text.p: Testing windy conditions could not stop Wimbledon champion and top seed Richard Krajicek advancing to the semifinals of the $1.22 million Japan Open on Friday.
Despite frequent strong gusts, the Dutchman served significantly better than in his two previous matches to complete a 6-4 6-3 quarter-final victory over eighth seed David Prinosil of Germany.
The wind also introduced elements of farce into the match involving Krajicek's semifinal opponent Patrick Rafter and fellow Autralian Todd Woodbridge.
Both players had to wait between serves for gusts to die down and play was halted repeatedly by windblown objects, including Rafter's hat, a net post, ballboys' kneeling mats and plastic bags.
Rafter won 6-4 7-6, but has never beaten Krajicek in their six previous confrontations.
"I'm going to have to come up with something different this time and hopefully it'll happen for me," Rafter said.
